Floor held at 19; the entire global.c decision procedure is now read, measured and closed — the residual $s0/$s1 inversion needs the walk pointer at >=14 RA-time refs (has 5, ceiling 8 by partition me

F4 (byte-neutral reference lift by duplication into arms) KILLED on both shapes this CFG admits — cross-jump re-merges neither (+2 / +39 insns) and the loop body's 6:4 arg0-to-walk reference ratio mak
F3 (permuter) KILLED: 89,084 iterations over two chassis produced zero score-improving finds, and a clean single-function permuter rig is now banked and reusable.

frontier.hypothesis: The twelve buffer accesses did not all exist as references to ONE pseudo at global_alloc time in the original compile; some reference was created after RA, or the original's flow-time counts differed for a reason not yet identified. This is now the leading explanation, because the three structural levers (s2 splitting, s3 duplication, s2 live-length inflation) and the whole random-search neighbourhood (s4) are all measured dead.
frontier.mechanism: allocno priority is computed from flow/sched-time counts, but the bytes we compare against are post-reorg. s2 checked reorg's delay-slot duplication (no 0xC($sN)/0x14($sN) sits in a delay slot in the target) and s3 checked cross-jump (it merges nothing here), but no per-insn provenance table has ever been built for the twelve accesses, and reload-generated address reloads have never been enumerated at all.
frontier.next_probe: Forensics modality: dump the full RTL insn stream at flow, sched and global_alloc for the candidate form (cc1 -da plus BB2_SCHED_DEBUG / BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG / BB2_RELOAD_DEBUG on the instrumented tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 — NOT build/cc1) and enumerate, insn by insn, every target byte whose reference could have been created after RA, including reload-generated address reloads. Deliverable is a per-insn provenance table for the 12 buffer accesses and the 5 walk accesses, which either finds the slack or proves the counts are pinned end to end.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is an artefact of having PATCHED an inherited body rather than re-derived the function: a from-scratch reconstruction of func_80078654 from the target bytes may express the buffer or the walk in a partition no incremental edit of the current body can reach.
frontier.mechanism: Every form measured in s1-s4 is a local edit of one inherited body — and s4 now shows that even 89,084 random mutations stay inside that one dataflow neighbourhood, because the permuter mutates spellings rather than inventing a different decomposition. The priority model says the answer must lie in a different partition, so a re-derivation is the only systematic way to leave the neighbourhood.
frontier.next_probe: Rederive modality: run m2c on asm/funcs/func_80078654.s, write the reconstruction VERBATIM from its output (not from candidate.c), then measure sandbox and the BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG table. Compare the resulting pseudo partition against the target's, and specifically check whether the reconstruction expresses arg0 as a struct pointer with fewer distinct RA-time references, or expresses the walk with a second induction variable. The s4 rig (tmp/grind/func_80078654/s4/mkws.sh) can then permute the reconstruction cheaply — a re-derived chassis is the one seed s4 did not have.

frontier.hypothesis: Directed permutation (hand-written PERM_* macros over the specific alternatives the technique rules name) is materially different from the random mutation s4 measured and may still reach the flip.
frontier.mechanism: Random mode samples spellings uniformly; PERM_GENERAL / PERM_LINESWAP let a form enumerate a chosen cross-product exhaustively, so a small set of semantically-equivalent alternatives is covered completely rather than sampled. tools/permuter_annotate.py is the bridge, though its hint catalog does not currently carry an entry that fits this function (no returns to vary, loop-rotation already killed in s1).
frontier.next_probe: LOW priority — record it as measured-thin rather than untried: the s4 evidence is that every spelling-preserving edit leaves the two reference counts pinned, so a directed sweep over spellings is predicted dead by the same model. Only worth running on a RE-DERIVED chassis (frontier 2), where the alternatives being enumerated are genuine partition choices rather than spellings, and it should be seeded with hand-written PERM_GENERAL blocks rather than permuter_annotate.py.
